t: A modern 8-bit chip with built-in amplifiers and mixed-voltage pins.
steps: Buy an AVR128DB48 Curiosity Nano from an electronics distributor.
Install the free Arduino IDE on your computer.
Add the DxCore board package through the Boards Manager.
Plug the Curiosity Nano into your computer with a micro-USB cable.
Choose the AVR DB-series board and the AVR128DB48 chip in the board menu.
Pick the onboard nEDBG debugger as the programmer.
Open the Blink example and press Upload. The LED on the kit starts to blink.
meta: Open Board. From $3.95. A few stores.
